name: Relentlessly push boundaries
definition: Always ask, "How can this be better?" "How will we win?" Know when to balance delivery with perfection.

rows.situation: Asking how this can be better
rows.under: Accepts the current design as good enough. Does not ask the next question.
rows.justRight: Always asks how this can be better. Looks for the change that would actually raise the bar.
rows.over: Asks the question so often that nothing ships. Better becomes a reason to restart.

rows.under: Plans as if the competition will wait. Cannot say what winning looks like.
rows.justRight: Asks how we will win, and uses the answer to choose the work. Knows what would make the outcome matter.
rows.over: Treats every project as a war. Winning talk replaces a real plan.

rows.under: Ships the first draft and calls it done. Quality is someone else's problem.
rows.justRight: Knows when to balance delivery with perfection. Ships when the next increment of polish will not change the outcome.
rows.over: Holds the work until it is perfect. The window closes.

rows.under: Treats the first limit as the last word. Stops at the obvious boundary.
rows.justRight: Pushes the boundary that can actually move. Tests whether the constraint is real before accepting it.
rows.over: Pushes every boundary, including the ones that protect the product or the customer.

rows.situation: Raising the ambition of the work
rows.under: Takes the smallest version of the problem. Never asks what a much larger outcome would require.
rows.justRight: Raises the ambition when the current plan cannot win. Makes the bigger version concrete enough to start.
rows.over: Announces a much larger goal with no path. Ambition becomes a slide.
